news.title: OpenAI 发布 Images 2.6 并向所有档位开放 Codex
news.originalTitle: Images 2.6 is available today in ChatGPT, and Codex across all tiers on web, desktop, and mobile.
news.summary: OpenAI 宣布 Images 2.6 今日起在 ChatGPT 中可用，Codex 同时面向所有档位开放，覆盖 web、桌面和移动端。GPT-Image-2.6 Flare 和 Sunburst 也已在 API 中提供，详情见官方页面 https://openai.com/index/introducing-images-2-6/。

news.title: OpenAI 发布 GPT-Image-2.6 Flare 与 Sunburst 两款开发者图像模型
news.originalTitle: Two new image models for developers: GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst.
news.summary: OpenAI 发布面向开发者的两款新图像模型 GPT-Image-2.6 Flare 和 Sunburst。Flare 最快六秒即可生成图像；Sunburst 主打更高质量的生成和跨编辑的一致性。两者还支持图像标记与 SVG 导出，便于进一步精修和使用生成结果。

news.title: ChatGPT Images 2.6 支持生成动图 GIF
news.originalTitle: GIFS!
news.summary:
GIF 动图！

用 ChatGPT Images 2.6，把提示词或图片变成动态 GIF。

可调整速度、编辑单帧，还能循环分享。

news.title: OpenAI 发布 ChatGPT Images 2.6，新增 GIF 与参考图功能
news.originalTitle: Images, upgraded—introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6.
news.summary: OpenAI 发布 ChatGPT Images 2.6，新增 GIF 和参考图功能。同时宣布两款新模型即将登陆 API，图像生成速度提升 50%。

news.title: OpenAI API 支持标注图像编辑
news.originalTitle: You can now send a marked-up image to the API to show exactly where you want an edit.
news.summary:
现在你可以向 API 发送带标注的图像，准确指出想要编辑的位置。

对于大多数编辑，先从低复杂度开始。如果场景包含多个元素或需要权衡多项约束，可尝试中或高复杂度，给模型更多规划空间。

按所需细节程度单独设置图像质量。

news.title: OpenAI 教你用静态角色制作循环 GIF
news.originalTitle: Bring a still character, sprite, or mascot to life as a looping GIF for a video, game, or app.
news.summary:
把静态角色、精灵图或吉祥物做成循环 GIF，用于视频、游戏或应用。

从美术素材开始，描述你想要的动效。试试挥手、回头或胜利舞，并让动作循环回起始姿势。

news.title: OpenAI 介绍 GPT Image 2.6 Flare 低画质下最快六秒生成图像
news.originalTitle: With image quality set to low, Flare can generate an image in as little as six seconds.
news.summary: OpenAI 介绍 GPT Image 2.6 Flare 在画质设为 low 时最快六秒即可生成一张图像。引用 @DesignArena 数据称，GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst 在 Image Arena 排名第一，超过前代 2.5 Sunburst，其中 2.6 Flare 比前代快 2.6 倍，2.6 Sunburst 快 1.15 倍。

news.title: OpenAI 将 GPT-Image-2.6 引入 Codex 和 API
news.originalTitle: Today, we’re bringing GPT-Image-2.6 to Codex and the API.
news.summary: OpenAI 将 GPT-Image-2.6 引入 Codex 和 API。新 API 图像模型 Flare 和 Sunburst 生成速度比之前快 50%；在 medium 或 high 质量下，Sunburst 能在多次编辑间保持细节更一致。

news.title: OpenAI 与 Linux 维护者及 Patch the Planet 合作发现并修复漏洞
news.originalTitle: Our goal is to help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities before attackers can use them. We’re working with Linux maintainers and Patch ...
news.summary: OpenAI 表示其目标是帮助防御者在攻击者利用之前发现并修复漏洞，正在与 Linux 维护者和 Patch the Planet 合作伙伴合作提交漏洞报告和补丁，详情见 openai.com/index/a-thousand-fewer-paths-to-root/。

news.title: OpenAI 公布 AI 挖掘本地提权漏洞成本：约 $1,279 一个漏洞
news.originalTitle: The full run cost $1,213,430 in API credits—about $1,279 per distinct local privilege escalation vulnerability.
news.summary: OpenAI 公布一次漏洞挖掘运行的数据：全程 API 调用花费 $1,213,430，平均每个本地提权（local privilege escalation）漏洞成本约 $1,279。按历史 Pwn2Own 和 TyphoonPWN 赏金标准折算，这些漏洞的假设价值为 $18.9M–$66.3M，OpenAI 据此认为防御方应主动用 AI 分析软件，使网络攻击的成本高到难以承受。

news.title: OpenAI 展示模型复现 1,724 个漏洞并生成 948 个本地提权可用 exploit
news.originalTitle: The run reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities. It produced proofs of concept for 291 information leaks and working exploits for 948 distinct l...
news.summary: OpenAI 介绍一次运行复现了 1,724 个漏洞，为 291 个信息泄露生成了概念验证，并为 948 个不同的本地提权漏洞生成了可用 exploit。这些 exploit 在开启标准安全防护的原始 Linux 桌面配置上可以运行。

news.title: OpenAI 称其智能体发现至少 10 种新型 Linux 漏洞利用技术
news.originalTitle: The agents also discovered and used at least 10 Linux exploitation techniques that, to the best of our knowledge and all of the experts t...
news.summary: OpenAI 称其智能体发现并使用了至少 10 种新型 Linux 漏洞利用技术，据其及所咨询专家所知均为此前未知的。OpenAI 认为这表明前沿大语言模型能发现并修补新的漏洞利用方式，而不只是套用已知技术。
news.reason: OpenAI 称其智能体发现了至少 10 种此前未知的 Linux 漏洞利用技术，并讨论前沿模型对新型漏洞利用能力的含义。

news.title: OpenAI 展示自主漏洞发现与修补管线，一次运行生成 948 个 Linux 内核本地提权漏洞补丁
news.originalTitle: Our security researchers built an autonomous cyber vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patching pipeline.
news.summary: OpenAI 安全研究人员构建了自主的网络漏洞发现、利用与修补管线，用一款即将推出的网络安全模型在单次运行中验证并为 Linux 内核 948 个本地提权漏洞生成补丁，总 API 成本 120 万美元。漏斗数据显示：2,308 个候选发现中 1,724 个通过验证，最终得到 948 个可用的 LPE exploit 和 291 个可用的 PoC。

news.title: 彭博社称苹果收紧员工 AI 使用预算，部分工程师日额度下降 33%
news.originalTitle: 彭博社称苹果收紧员工 AI 使用预算：部分工程师日额度下降 33%，恐进一步下探至 100 美元
news.summary: 彭博社报道称苹果为遏制 AI 使用成本，削减员工调用 AI 工具的内部预算，部分工程师每日 AI 支出上限已从 300 美元降至 200 美元，最低可能进一步降至每日 100 美元，非工程团队额度甚至考虑压低至 25 美元，有更高需求者可向高级管理层申请豁免。

news.title: AI 相关政治行动委员会投入数百万美元影响美国中期选举但成效不一

news.title: Qualcomm 押注数据中心芯片，预计最终占业务 30%

news.summary: Qualcomm 在 Q4 2026 财报电话会上表示，数据中心芯片最终将占其业务约 30%。在智能手机销量较 2025 年下滑约 20% 的背景下，公司预计 2027 年 Q1 数据中心收入约 6.5 亿美元，2027 年底达 50 亿美元，2029 年达 150 亿美元，并已与 Amazon 和 Meta 达成合作。相比 AMD 预计数据中心最终贡献超 80% 收入，其目标相对保守。

news.title: Uber 财报电话会披露：AI 智能体下单量极低，万圣节周仅 4 次用车订单
news.originalTitle: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says
news.summary: Uber 在三季度财报电话会上表示，10 月最繁忙的万圣节周仅 4 次用车由 AI 智能体下单，Uber Eats 也只有 500 单智能体订单，同期平台总订单量约 3.2 亿。CEO Dara Khosrowshahi 称目前仍非常早期，并指出 App 内叫车平均只需 50 秒、再点常点餐食约 90 秒，智能体未必省时；DoorDash 上周也称至今仅收到几百单智能体订单。

news.title: The Verge 评论马斯克 4.46 亿美元竞选支出打水漂：问题出在 X 信息茧房

news.title: Stanford 研究测算 NVIDIA B200 每单位能量产出价值超 AMD MI350X 4 倍
news.originalTitle: Stanford's new research: The NVIDIA B200 delivered over 4x the dollar value and over 9x the expert time saved per unit of energy compared...
news.summary: Stanford 研究者在 220 个真实专业任务上用同一模型 Qwen3.6-27B 测试 4 种单颗 AI 芯片，衡量每单位能量产生的有用工作。结果显示 NVIDIA B200 相比 AMD MI350X 每单位能量带来超过 4 倍的美元价值和超过 9 倍的专家时间节省，即模型不变、仅换芯片也会显著改变同样电力预算下的经济回报。作者引用的论文还构建了 Joules-to-GDP 指标，测试 5 个开源模型，其中 Gemma 4 31B 用 23% 的能量达到 GLM 5.2 每任务净价值的 56%，Qwen3.6-27B 从 1 卡 H100 扩到 8 卡仅快 22% 却耗能 3.2 倍。

news.title: Perplexity 将 Fast Search 接入 Decisions API

news.summary: 我们正在将 Perplexity 的 Fast Search 集成到 Perplexity Decisions API 中。这使得批量决策能够基于来自网络的事实依据来做出。业界领先且最快的 API。搜索每次请求收费 $0.001，Decisions API 每 1M 输入 token 收费 $0.02。

news.title: Stanford 论文提出 Joules-to-GDP 框架：小模型每单位能量的经济回报可远超最强模型
news.originalTitle: New Stanford paper finds that a smaller AI model can return far more economic value per unit of energy than the most capable one.
news.summary: Stanford 团队发布 Joules-to-GDP 框架，以扣除运行成本后每焦耳能量的净经济价值衡量 AI 工作，测试 5 个开源模型在 GDPval 220 个任务、44 个职业上的表现。

news.title: Anthropic 用 Claude 绘制细菌 vault 粒子首个 3D 结构
news.originalTitle: Anthropic’s biology lab used Claude to find and map a vault particle, a hollow barrel of protein that has sat unexplained in human cells ...
news.summary: Anthropic 生物学研究团队分享与 Claude 合作完成细菌来源 vault 粒子首个 3D 结构测定的过程。Vault 粒子是 1986 年发现的大型桶状蛋白结构，功能至今未知；此前只见于动物和植物等复杂生命，团队证明细菌及其病毒中的类似蛋白也能组装成 vault。Claude 在部分环节大幅提速，人工测定结构需数周到数月，该项目只用数天，但也出现一些简单错误，团队与机器学习研究者协作修正。作者补充称 Claude 实际运行了湿实验室流程，将粒子分离从 3 天缩短到约 90 分钟，34 小时内给出首个 3D 结构模型。

news.title: Cognition 推出 SWE-2 Flash 编码模型
news.originalTitle: Introducing SWE-2 Flash, our new fast & efficient coding model.
news.summary:
推出 SWE-2 Flash，我们全新的快速高效编码模型。

在领先评测中，它超越了所有美国开放权重模型，甚至包括规模大 3 倍的模型。

Voyager 是一款桌面 AI 智能体，它介于 Seedance 2.5 等 AI 视频模型与 Blender、DaVinci Resolve、Premiere Pro 等专业剪辑软件之间。

news.title: Apple Intelligence 国行版登陆 iOS 27.3 beta，由千问替代 ChatGPT 角色
news.originalTitle: Apple Intelligence is live in China on iOS 27.3 beta, with Alibaba's Qwen where ChatGPT sits.
news.summary: Apple Intelligence 已在 iOS 27.3 beta 中国区上线，由阿里千问（Qwen）承担 ChatGPT 在其他市场的位置。设置分两步：开启 Apple Intelligence（约 7GB 端侧模型下载）后授权 Qwen。实测中仅当本地模型无法完成的任务才调用 Qwen，部分任务会跳转到其 App。

想调准你的语音方向，试试在 @GoogleAIStudio 里用“Remix this voice”🪄

在那里，你可以并排试听三个生成的版本，挑选喜欢的继续重混，并保存下来以便在不同脚本和多说话人场景中复用。

news.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS 上线 Voice Remixing，支持用提示词微调声音

news.title: Viggle 发布视频转换 Agent Viggle Remake 并开放权重

news.title: 数据中心成为美国中期选举输家：多州候选人支持暂停建设
news.originalTitle: Data centers lost the midterms
news.summary: The Verge 报道称，数据中心开发商在美国中期选举后面临更受限的建设环境，投票者选择了支持暂停建设或设置更多扩建障碍的候选人。NBC News 民调显示 76% 的受访者反对在所在社区建数据中心；全国 45 项地方 ballot 措施中，33 项结果将限制数据中心开发，如俄亥俄多市禁止超过 25MW 的数据中心。

news.title: Thinking Machines 发布 Inkling 2 Small，权重将开源为评分最高的中国以外开放权重模型

news.title: Goodfire 提出 mechanistic shaping 框架 用内部表征抑制模型走捷径
news.originalTitle: Shaping and Monitoring Models Through Their Internal Representations
news.summary: Goodfire Research 发布论文提出 mechanistic shaping 框架，通过 reliance shaping 和 expression shaping 在训练中惩罚模型对特定内部概念的依赖或表达，使模型以正确方式解题而非仅答对。
news.reason: 论文提出用模型内部表征直接指定解题方式的训练框架，并系统评估了这么做之后监控探针如何退化与恢复。

news.title: Anthropic 研究 20.7 万会话中科研人员如何使用 Claude
news.originalTitle: AI for scientific discovery: How researchers use Claude
news.summary: Anthropic 用隐私保护方法分析 2026 年 8 月 2 日至 9 月 30 日的 207,049 个 Claude 与 Claude Code 科研会话，发现科学家主要用于数据分析（占 Claude 会话 33.7%、Claude Code 48.1%）和写作，而构思与数据收集的使用低于其重要性排名。
news.reason: 基于隐私保护的 20.7 万会话分析，给出了科研任务使用分布与加速情景，读者可据此对照自身领域的 AI 采用空间。

news.title: NVIDIA 如何通过协同设计最大化 AI 工厂中每个字节的价值
news.originalTitle: Five Ways NVIDIA Co-Design Maximizes the Value of Every Byte in the AI Factory
news.summary: NVIDIA 详解其协同设计如何最大化 AI 工厂中每个字节的价值：从 GB300 NVL72 到 Vera Rubin NVL72，HBM 容量维持 288 GB 而带宽升至 19.2 TB/s，在 SemiAnalysis AgentX 上实现最高 30 倍的每兆瓦吞吐提升。NVFP4 将模型占用较 FP16 缩减约 3.5 倍，KV cache 占用较 FP8 减少最高 50%。

source.name: NVIDIA Technical Blog：Agentic AI / Generative AI

news.reason: METR 基于高权限访问逐条对比公开与未删减报告，指出 2x 加速阈值的判断依据被弱化，读者可借此校准对风险报告措辞的解读。

news.title: Anthropic 发布 FlashProve 原型，用 zkSNARK 验证 AI 响应来自指定模型而不暴露权重
news.originalTitle: Anthropic's new prototype proves which model wrote an AI response without exposing its weights
news.summary: Anthropic 发布开源研究原型 FlashProve，用 zkSNARK 密码学证明 AI 响应确实来自声明的模型，且不暴露模型权重。在单张 H100 上对 4000 亿参数的 Llama 4 Maverick 生成证明约 110 tokens 每秒，每份证明约 19 MB，普通 CPU 上 17 秒可验证，开销约为正常推理的 70x 至 95x。

news.title: 科技并购基金还撑得住吗？a16z 对比私募股权与风投的周期困境
news.originalTitle: Is Private Equity Cooked?
news.summary: a16z 发文分析科技并购（tech buyout）为何正陷入结构性困境：2026 年上半年风投基金将科技公司估值上调 16%，并购基金却下调 4%。过去十年美国并购基金年化回报 14.5%，落后于 Russell 3000，而同期美国风投整体年化 17.6%；并购退出周期已从 2010–21 年的 5–6 年拉长到约 7 年。

news.title: 2026 美国中期选举出口民调显示 AI 和数据中心在选民议题中排名末位

news.title: Together AI 提出 Polymorphic Inference：面向开放模型的自调优推理

news.summary: Tomasz Tunguz 分析认为 2027 年美国 AI 算力上限约 80GW，即一年内新建相当于历史上全部算力规模的容量。短期 GPU 租金六个月内从每小时 $3 涨到 $12-13，Anthropic 混合 GPU 成本两个季度上升 82%，已建成机架因缺电无法启用；他推算理论收入上限接近 $500b，并提出效率将成为全栈主导主题。

news.title: 斯坦福 RoboArchitect：编码模型自动重写机器人控制代码
news.originalTitle: New Stanford paper shows that robot control code no longer needs hand-building for each new robot, because a coding model can diagnose fa...
news.summary: 斯坦福论文提出 RoboArchitect，用编码模型审查机器人试跑记录、诊断失败并最多迭代 5 轮重写控制代码，全程不更新模型权重，单次完整运行平均成本低于 150 美元。在未见场景上平均成功率从裸策略的 9.7% 升至 43.3%，未见任务上从 12.7% 升至 40.2%。在 VLABench 上，加装控制代码的通用策略击败了在该基准上微调的同款策略，但所有测试均在仿真中完成。

news.title: Canva 十年来首次增长放缓，裁员及岗位调整涉及 22% 员工
news.originalTitle: Bloomberg: Canva’s growth slowed for the first time in a decade, and its response affects 1,271 people, 22% of staff, through layoffs, ro...
news.summary: 据 Bloomberg，Canva 十年来首次增长放缓，为此进行的大调整涉及 1271 人，占员工的 22%，形式包括裁员、岗位变动或搬迁。官方未将 AI 列为裁员原因，报道指调整旨在让 Canva 具备构建 AI 产品的能力，而非用自动化替代离职员工的工作；但成本制约了这一计划，因面向大量非付费用户的服务成本过高，Canva 已推迟多个 AI 产品发布。

news.title: Meta 发行 150 亿美元债券投向 AI 建设，认购订单达 580 亿美元

news.summary: Meta 为 AI 基础设施建设发行 150 亿美元美元债券，认购订单达 580 亿美元，约为发行规模的 3.9 倍，与今年主要科技债券发售水平相当。Meta 预计三年内在 AI 上支出超过 7400 亿美元，属于业内规模最大的算力投入计划之一；2025 年以来 Meta 已发债约 700 亿美元，在大型科技公司中排名第三，仅次于 Alphabet 和 Amazon。

news.title: Anthropic 研究开源系统 FlashProve，用密码学证明 AI 模型输出身份
news.originalTitle: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
news.summary: Anthropic 发布研究博客，介绍开源系统 FlashProve，通过密码学证明验证某个输出确实来自特定模型，技术规范和代码已在 GitHub 公开。系统要求模型发布方公开不泄露权重的模型指纹，可在本地设备完成验证，可用于防止实验室偷偷换用更便宜或更贵的模型，但暂无在 Anthropic 或其他实验室部署的计划。

news.summary: SemiAnalysis 分析称 SpaceX 已有 3.6GW 数据中心容量在建，并将 2027 年目标上调至约 13GW，可能成为全球最快的数据中心建设者。文章拆解 Colossus 2、Starbase、TeraFab 等站点进度，指出其改造项目 91 天完成 210MW，并靠 Tesla 生产的模块化 MEP 设备、约 6GWh BESS 和并网来补齐约 300MW 的电力缺口。

news.title: 乌克兰无人机打击促使俄罗斯企业计划将数据中心转入地下
news.originalTitle: Ukraine’s drone strikes spur hasty Russian plans for underground data centers
news.summary: 乌克兰无人机打击损毁了 Yandex、Sberbank、VKontakte 和俄财政部运行的数据中心，干扰了数百万俄用户的云服务，俄方企业开始寻求将数据中心加固并转入地下。据俄媒 Vedomosti 报道，国营电信公司 Rostelcom 正与矿业公司 Norilsk 商讨将部分数据中心移入地下；克里姆林宫还要求数据中心业主为紧急国家需求预留算力，并授权可能使用境外数据中心。

news.title: 乌克兰无人机打击促使俄方筹划地下数据中心并征用算力
news.originalTitle: Ukraine’s drone strikes spur hasty Russian plans for underground data centers
news.summary: 乌克兰无人机打击损坏了存放 AI 超级计算机的设施，扰乱了数百万俄罗斯用户的云服务，俄罗斯科技公司正计划将数据中心加固或转入地下。受打击的数据中心涉及 Yandex、Sberbank、VKontakte 和俄罗斯财政部；国有电信公司 Rostelecom 与 Norilsk 探讨将部分数据中心移入地下，克里姆林宫要求数据中心所有者为紧急国家需求预留算力，并批准可能使用境外数据中心。

news.title: 哈佛MIT论文：推理模型思维链难控源于“Okay”开头习惯
news.originalTitle: New Harvard and MIT paper finds that reasoning models' poor control over their chain-of-thought partly comes from a habit of opening it w...
news.summary: 哈佛与MIT论文发现，推理模型对思维链控制不佳部分源于习惯以“Okay”开头。Qwen3-32B和OLMo-3.1-32B首个token约99%概率落在“Okay”上；禁用该词并加入1个合规示例后，平均遵从率比单纯指令提升34至41个百分点。隐藏信息类任务（如避免某词）响应不一致，在12个模型中似属独立能力。

news.title: NVFP4量化让视频模型提速且不掉质量
news.originalTitle: (3/6) 4-bit without the quality hit.
news.summary:
(3/6) 4-bit 量化，质量不打折。

NVFP4 QAD 以 BF16 Flex 为蒸馏目标，与它的差距比普通量化缩小 14-17%。

长片段受限于注意力计算，因此 FP4 注意力将 768p 15 秒的耗时从 101.8 秒降至 85.3 秒。

news.title: Stanford 研究：44% 被广泛引用的 LLM 结论已失效，推理类缺陷消失最快
news.originalTitle: Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds
news.summary: Stanford 研究者 Owen Queen 和 James Zou 用 2024 年 7 月至 2026 年 9 月间八家开发商的 20 个模型检验 50 条广被引用的 LLM 结论，发现 44% 已失效，34% 明显减弱，仅 16% 仍成立。

news.title: AI 个人软件方向之辩
news.originalTitle: I used to think personal software built with AI was the future. Everyone builds their own Figma, Linear, video editor, etc.
news.summary:
我曾以为用 AI 构建个人软件是未来。每个人都构建自己的 Figma、Linear、视频编辑器等等。

我现在觉得这不对了。为当下任务而生的短生命周期专用软件，似乎更有可能，配合单一数据存储来保存事实来源/结果/输出。尤其是随着模型变得更好更快。

如果你是构建者，请为互操作性而构建。

source.name: X：Ado Kukic（Anthropic 开发者关系，Claude Code） (@adocomplete)

news.title: Claude Code 新增跳过权限与后台超时设置
news.originalTitle: Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. That’s intentional, but if you’re in a...
news.summary:
即使在 bypass permissions 模式下，Claude Code 在运行少数风险特别高的 rm 命令前仍会询问。这是有意为之，但如果你身处一次性容器中、且可以接受这些命令不经询问直接运行，现在可以设置 CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=1。

而超时的 shell 命令现在会在后台继续运行，而不是被中断，因此长时间的构建或测试套件不会在中途被杀掉。

news.title: Claude 云端会话与 API 额度更新
news.originalTitle: And a few smaller ones:
news.summary:
还有几个较小的更新：

- 云端会话现在会在你还在输入提示词时就开始设置，因此你点击发送后的等待时间更短
- 你可以点击云端会话 diff 中的任意一行并留下评论，它会随你的下一条消息一起发送给 Claude
- Max、Ultra 和 Team 套餐现在每月包含 API 额度，可用于通过 Claude API 和 Agent SDK 进行构建
- 支持该功能的 MCP 服务器可以在任务进行中向你提出后续问题，并在后台运行长时间任务

news.title: Claude 新增 effort 控制与 /usage 用量诊断
news.originalTitle: You also get a bit more control over Claude's effort.
news.summary: Claude 新增更细的 effort 控制：在消息中输入 ultrathink 可将单轮 effort 临时提升至 xhigh，无需改动整个会话的设置。用户还可为 subagent 单独指定 effort 级别，例如会话为 high 时让子智能体以 medium 运行。CLI 的 /usage 现在会用直白语言说明是什么在消耗额度，若有快速修复可按 f 直接应用。

news.title: Claude Code 优化闲置会话压缩并在 Pro/Max 增加用量提醒

news.summary: Claude Code 现在会在 prompt cache 约一小时过期前自动压缩长时间闲置的会话，之后恢复时只需重新处理摘要而非整段对话，降低用量消耗。此外在 Pro 和 Max 套餐上，恢复超长对话若会占用 5 小时限额的较大比例，会先给出提醒。

AI 让写代码变得极快，但在生产环境运行这些代码并没有变得更容易。

tweets.text:
If you are a product leader, here is a simple exercise: draw out your product lifecycle.

e.g. market understanding -> design -> development -> GTM.

Chances are your PMs spend more time in some stages than others - because of the nature of your product, your org or their comfort zones.

This is a handoff-heavy, lossy process.

Now ask yourself: using AI, how much deeper can PMs go on every stage?

PMs should be able to
- build a much deeper, broader understanding of users and the market
- iterate fast from ideas to working prototypes
- explore the codebase to study technical constraints and tradeoffs
- run their own analytics and investigate questions as they emerge
- understand the GTM funnel deeply enough to shape product strategy

Now, this is not about PMs replacing every role. As the function that spans the entire lifecycle, this is about  raising the bar on the PM role, so they combine their breadth with much greater depth.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.role: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

tweets.text:
It turns out the advancements we’re getting in coding and computer use, combined with industry specific understand and general reasoning, can bring automation to a large number of areas of knowledge work.

We’re entering the era of autonomous collaborators in a number of industries that haven’t yet had their claude code or codex moment yet. But now this is going to happen. 

We’ll see it in animation, film production, gaming, manufacturing, architecture, product design, robotics, and more. All of these fields have the potential of driving far more output similar to what we’ve seen in software engineering. There’s no inherent finite demand for these categories of work.

“Software is eating the world” is finally in a much bigger way happening because of AI.

We’re moving from an era of AI where the output comes roughly at the rate that you can chat back and forth with the AI to work with you, to a period where you can set a problem for a set of agents to go off and do an arbitrarily large amount of work for you. This means productivity gains that are maybe 20-50% to gains that don’t really have an upper limit.

Agent swarms and the ability to fan out complex work across many agents doing tasks in parallel provide a massive unlock in a lot of spaces. This will lead to qualitatively different outcomes in my fields. 

This has already been seen across the coding domain. Next, cyber is almost entirely a problem space where more agents reviewing more things will lead to far better outcomes. We’re seeing the same now in many scientific fields, and this almost certainly will change life sciences. 

But this will increasingly be true in any field where you can parallelize computer-based work to complete something faster or do something at a totally different quality level. Which is actually are some of the most valuable domains of knowledge work today. 

Our brains aren’t really wired for the new scenario we’re heading into where compute becomes the variable that we can flex to solve any problem that we want. We’re used to thinking that the amount of time that goes into a task is correlated to the output that we get from it. And most domains of knowledge work or science have generally always been correlated with this. That’s changing forever.

A good lesson in AI is that you need to check back in on the latest with every 3 to 6 months to try something that wasn’t possible before and see if it works again.

At no point in AI’s history is that more true than today. Just the past six months of model progress around computer and tool use, less context rot, better reasoning, multimodality, and deeper domain expertise in a number of key fields, these models are vastly more capable on what they can execute.

This is opening up a new vector of what AI systems will be able to autonomously work on. Essentially, anything with an API (and even many things without), we can anticipate that an agent will be able to control and utilize as an underlying capability to complete a process.

This means that we are no longer dependent on *just* the models generating everything from whole cloth, but instead they can fully utilize existing systems (or new ones purpose built for them) very effectively. This creates immense leverage for agents.

Security agents can leverage existing data feeds and cyber tooling, IT agents that can execute workflows reliably across software stacks, data agents that can migrate data or processes between systems, architect and design agents can leverage CAD and design tools, and on and on. And any of today’s tools that don’t work will likely be replaced by agent-friendly or OSS tooling that does the same. 

When you combine this with the domain understanding being trained into agents, you started to get autonomous collaborators for every job function and industry. This will open up a ton of new opportunities in AI if you build with this understanding in mind.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch

tweets.text:
So bullish on MCP. Its utility exceeds the "M" part: even AI aside, it'll be a civilization-scale accomplishment to get all our systems communicating through one universal open protocol.

A missing piece was how to get arbitrary callbacks across sessions. MCP could read and write, but it couldn't tell you later "this event happened." MCP Events fixes this.

We're adding support in our own MCP. Say an agent makes a deployment, and wants to know when it's complete. Instead of polling, it can subscribe to 𝚍𝚎𝚙𝚕𝚘𝚢𝚖𝚎𝚗𝚝.𝚜𝚞𝚌𝚌𝚎𝚎𝚍𝚎𝚍.

PSA: With Vercel Queues and Workflows, writing the backend machinery for your own MCPs to do this is easy peasy.

At @vercel we got to test this model before release. Best way to summarize it: astonishingly brilliant.

One interesting takeaway: it's very clear that this new generation of models can take on unprecedented bodies of parallel work.

To actually seize this intelligence, you need cloud sandboxes. Full stop. The model can delegate and orchestrate far more than a single computer can handle. Likely far more than you can even imagine it can handle.

Your bottleneck is now ① your ambition and ② your parallel computing power.

Btw, I learned from @cramforce you don't need to overcomplicate it. Install Vercel CLI, setup the Plugin and tell the agent to use /𝚘𝚏𝚏𝚕𝚘𝚊𝚍-𝚝𝚘-𝚜𝚊𝚗𝚍𝚋𝚘𝚡 skill. It'll provision and de-allocate cloud sandboxes as needed. You don't need a "multi-agent remote harness ralph orchestrator" 😆

Built a physical simulation of a record player with WebGL2 and Web Audio. It's *shockingly* accurate: https://t.co/MBNaTfKoai.

Instead of playing a song, it works by converting it into the physical shape of a groove. Then a simulated stylus rides those walls 384,000 times a second, and you hear the voltage that motion would induce in a cartridge.

So the crackle, the pops, the wow/flutter, the dull inner grooves are natural byproducts of the simulation. You can also "DJ" the record.

(The converted songs are in the public domain or CC-licensed. Code is linked for you to remix and re-deploy.)

The first version was live in 3 days, and we immediately used it for our internal show-and-tell. This feels like a new era of professionals building their own professional tools, tailored to exactly how they work.

• Games and design: @jackcheng gave it a photo of his toddler’s messy playroom. It turned the actual toys into a playable racing game, with fun details like a stray shoe as an obstacle and a sippy cup as a power-up.

• Knowledge work: @hammer_mt turned his research into a documentary. The model came up with interview questions, he answered them on camera, and it cut the footage together. He called this the most productive 3 weeks of his career.

• A different way of working: Give it a big job and leave it running overnight or over a weekend. But tell it what “done” means: Mike found it could finish the build, then spend another day or two testing. Set the goal, the budget, and how much checking you need before walking away.

• The catch: It’s slow and burns through tokens. Our early-access usage was free, and these projects would have been expensive at API rates. It’s 20% cheaper than Fable 5.1, but for everyday writing, emails, or quick back-and-forth coding, I’d usually reach for something else.

The clearest signal: When our early access ended, @TylerNishida stopped working on some projects until he could get this model back. He didn’t want to build them with anything else.

The best measure of a new model is whether it makes you try things you wouldn’t have tried before.

Fable 5.2 absolutely does that.

Ever since I read Niklas Gruhn's excellent article (https://t.co/ojHWKndeEL), I think about this every day..

If you don't think people notice that you are feeding everything to AI and regurgitating it back, people actually do!!

(because they are probably already getting an opinion with the same agents)

If you are visiting SF, and trying to meet more people, here are a random list of things you should remove from your vocabulary..

> swap notes
> "synergies"
> pick your brain
> networking
> "san fran" (tourist tell)
> grab coffee if you're free

If you want to meet interesting people here, show your work. The most interesting people I know in the city are not attending that fancy large conference - they are probably at their office. 

So what's the work? It can be as simple as a thoughtful cold email, a five line pointed DM, or complex as some side projects that you have shipped, or a meetup that you are organizing.

If you put in the effort, it shows, yes, even in this AI era. I still get so much slop across the board, that if I see anyone put in the effort, I try to go out of my way to meet them. 

Even the busiest people have 15 mins to give you, if you give them a reason to!

podcasts.titleZh: Handshake AI 深入拆解：前沿实验室到底在买什么样的数据
podcasts.summary: 本期访谈邀请 Handshake AI 创始人 Garrett Lord 及其团队，深入探讨前沿 AI 数据产业的演变。嘉宾指出，数据标注已从简单的画框、分类演变为由专家主导的环境构建、任务设计与评分标准编写，单个数据单元的制作可能耗时数天。团队依次展示了三个方向：生命科学基准 Vials 中模型解读化验图像的通过率不足五成（嘉宾说法）；金融基准 Atlas 中智能体在模拟投行任务里因一处税务处理错误污染整个模型；以及儿童安全基准 Care Bench 与企业对齐测试的发现。嘉宾认为数据市场三年内从十亿美元增长到百亿美元级别，且未来大部分数据工作将与安全对齐融合。
points: 嘉宾称数据标注已转变为专家“创作数据”：构建模拟环境、设计任务、编写数百行评分标准，一个数据单元的制作需要数天。
Vials 生命科学基准中，嘉宾表示各模型解读化验图像的整体正确率在50%以下，即使提供代码工具也不足60%。
Atlas 金融基准中嘉宾演示：智能体在2600多个公式的 LBO 模型里因未正确处理商誉税务处理，污染全部估值结果，多数受访银行家宁可从零重做。
Care Bench 覆盖12类儿童安全风险，嘉宾称父母与临床专家对模型行为的评判存在明显差异，模型拒绝后的“替代建议”被家长认为并不安全。
嘉宾预测数据市场三年内将达千亿美元规模，且未来大部分数据行业或与安全对齐行业合而为一。

podcasts.titleZh: 斯坦福如何教授 AI 原生软件工程
podcasts.summary: Mihail Eric 介绍斯坦福 CS 146S 课程的变化：从广泛介绍 AI 开发工具，转向上下文工程、设计与架构，以及在复杂代码库中解决实际问题。开篇也讨论了工程基础、开源贡献和维护者指导对学生成长的作用。
points: AI 开发工具的使用建立在软件工程基础之上，课程不替代算法等基础训练。
上下文工程、设计与架构成为处理复杂任务的重要内容。
真实开源贡献让学生接触大型代码库，并得到维护者的审查与指导。
podcasts.transcript:
Okay, this is a pretty special episode because we're celebrating one million subscribers on the AIU Code, uh, AI, AI Engineer YouTube channel. So go over there and subscribe if you haven't heard about it already.

The guest is Mihail Eric, who is not only teaching the Modern Software Developer at Stanford, which is going viral right now for basically covering all the AI-native development pract- best practices, uh, but also he is head of AI at Monaco.

So he's not only a teacher, but he's a practitioner. Um, and those of you coming to AIU Code Summit next week, um, it's gonna be the celebration of all the extreme progress that you've seen in coding in the last year.

I'm excited about all the themes of fighting slop, of system one models, and of increasing your ambition for major rewrites of basically everything that you've seen in code.

Um, there's never been a more exciting time to be an AI engineer, and with one million AI engineers, I think it's just getting started. So let's get into the interview.

Okay, we're in the studio with Mihail Eric, Adjunct Professor at Stanford and Head of AI at Monaco. Welcome. Thank you. I'm glad to be here.

You caught our attention because of your course that you are refreshing for the third time, third year? Second time. Second time? Yep. The CS 146, or 146S, the Modern Software Developer at Stanford.

This particular generation of junior developers, of junior engineers, the people that are now entering the workforce, will, I think, be the first kind of generation of that new shift.

And I looked at the syllabus, and I was like, "This is everything we cover." So every now and then, I like to invite people like yourself who, like, you cover a broad range of topics- Mm-hmm...

and then we can sort of go topic by topic and give people the state of the art- Yeah... on each of these things, which I, I assume you're doing with all your guests anyway. For sure. Tell us the history of the course.

What made you wanna spring out CS 146? Yeah. So this is the second time it's being taught, and I taught it for the first time last fall, so fall 2025. This was pre, like, Opus 4.5, 4.6 days.

But the-- Even before fall 2025, the course had been about, like, a year in the making.

The genesis of the class was like November of 2024, and I had sort of had this idea that we're seeing all this stuff happening in coding agents, and yes, they were an earlier version of the coding agents, but already it felt like there was something drastically changing in terms of how developers were doing their work, how quickly we were getting work done, uh, all that fun stuff.

And so at the time, I just-- It was all just scattered blog posts, scattered, like, things you could find online if you were trying to really get into the, the methodology of how to do these things.

And so I, I had this idea like, "Hey, well, is there a way to kind of structure a curriculum around this that's a little bit more formal?" Had the idea.

And you know, I, my alma mater is Stanford, and I always had this dream to go back and teach something and, and kind of pay it forward. Uh, I've always been very deep into education.

I talked to Chip, who also taught a class, uh, one of my good friends. Chip Hieatt. Yeah. Yeah, Chip Hieatt, exactly. Uh, spoke to her.

Who-- She had taught her, I guess, designing machine learning systems, and so, like, asked her what that process was like, and sort of, you know, took a lot of inspiration for how she-- from how she designed the curriculum and, and thought about, you know, getting something through the, through the school.

Put it together, spent about nine to ten months. This was now fall of 2024 through to, like, you know, mid to late of 2025. Got it through the committee, uh, made a case for the class to exist.

You know, I had to put together a proposal and everything. Uh, and that took me to fall 2025, when I taught it for the first time, which was very well-received. You know, students were really interested in it.

Uh, there was even, I guess, like, a Business Insider article that was written about the class last year. And then, yeah, this year, uh, a lot of things changed.

I would say really coding agents, autonomous coding agents really have picked up- [laughs]... in a way that, that we had not seen before.

Um, so it felt like it was time to do this again, uh, refresh things, uh, and here we are. M-Meanwhile, you're also head of AI at Monaco- Yeah... which is also a very buzzy startup. Yes, yes.

We are, we are, we are, we're in the airwaves right now and, and, uh, having a fun time doing it. Yeah. Yeah. Uh, so, like, I, I do like that you're also, I guess, a practitioner.

You guys are obviously implementing all this stuff at Monaco. Yeah. Any, I guess, principles or observations about just what you have changed from last year to this year at a high level? Yeah, yeah. I mean, a ton.

I think that

when I reflect on what last year's version of the class was, uh, I mean, coding agents had been around, but we were still in kind of that phase where companies were emerging that were tackling every single part of, like, the ISDLC.

There was, like, a coding agent for code review. There was a coding agent for, you know, spec design. There was a coding agent for, uh, SRE. And, you know, some of those-- Of course, some of those companies still exist.

But it felt like last year it was a lot more about a broad tour of here's everywhere you can use coding agents.

And in a way, a lot of the curriculum last year was, was geared toward exposure and this, this kind of survey, this kind of like odyssey of sorts through, hey, everything that you knew a-about the ISDLC is now changing because of AI.

Um, this year I think there's some principles that are solidifying, right? The idea of, like, very careful context engineering.

The idea of, like, really thinking through sort of like design and architecture as a way of handling really complex tasks. And so the nature of my class is it's not intended for the, like, beginner programmer.

It is not a, it is not a replacement for, like, traditional computer science in the sense of, like, algorithms and if-- In fact, a lot of those classes are prereqs to what I'm, what I'm doing here.

But I do know that you-- if you have a good foundation, going now toward applying that and, and, and sort of using those principles in, in production environments in, like, real world, that's something that I think is, is now at a place where...

You know, at Monaco, we deal with ma-massive code bases. You know, I help a lot of companies also with thinking through their massive code base, uh, designs and things like that.

And so really, it's more of a practitioner's course for once the students have graduated or are now entering the workforce, how to be the most productive members of, of the workforce. Yeah.

You said you're passionate about education. I feel like students in that phase of being in college are in a pretty interesting spot. Any advice and any takes? Should people study computer science right now?

Is cloud code and Codex all we need? Like, I, I wanna, you know, hear your thoughts. Yeah. I, uh, you know, there's a lot of anxiety from students, as you can probably imagine.

And, uh, and I, I think a lot of what I'm trying to communicate this time around is that the anxiety, a lot of it still is here, and there was anxiety last year as well.

But I wanna make the case that A well-trained AI native engineer, and I know that's like a buzzy word- [laughs]...

but let's say that we'll, we'll, we'll, we'll, we'll dive into maybe what aspects of that, that, that are most interesting.

A, like, well-trained and native engineer can be some of the most, you know, the most useful assets like any company around. And so,

and, and, you know, I-- this is the first week of class actually, and like week one, and you know, first lecture I'm like: Hey, I really believe that every company needs you, but the floor is much higher, right?

So you're entering as like your first job out of school, but it's not sufficient to just be like a, you know, an L3 in like a Google term if you're gonna use like that, that kind of leveling system there.

It's like you have to generally be better than, you know, almost at the senior level going into this. So like what, what can we-- how do we get there more quickly, right?

And so, uh, I'm trying to say that there is still a core bit of like foundational software engineering that is important to have some of these core values of, of sort of how software systems are built and the trade-offs of those systems.

But then beyond that, we go and, uh, you know, that's where I think you as the humans should still be valuable rather than... And the rest of the implementation details you can kind of defer more often. Hmm. Yeah.

Uh, this is something I've said before, which, uh, is, is almost like the controvers-- I, I-- it's, it's like the kind of thing you say to be spicy, but I almost, like I, I do genuinely kind of believe it, which is most students are cooked, some of them are [chuckles] gonna be super valuable.

I, I don't think it's a popular thing. This is a delicate topic. Stanford's, Stanford s- Stanford's kids are gonna be fine, right? They're from Stanford. Sure. But like what happens to like the rest of America?

[laughs] Right. Right. That, that, that is an open question. It's a weird situation- Yeah... 'cause I feel like a lot of education is slow to move. Like- Mm-hmm... I'm even curious in how,

how do you determine where do you put the end date to curriculum in a course on AI? Like- Oh my God... you're teaching a Stanford modern software- Ah... like that's changing every year. You cheat.

You just get the people from the co- uh, the coding agents to come and speak, right? [laughs] Oh, yeah. Like yeah, have them be the... Yeah. I-- that, that's a funny- The old guest lecturers. It's a funny... Well, yeah.

I mean, you know, that was, uh... Okay, so, so on, on the guest lecturers point, I think that was, um... I mean, that was also last year, um, that was also the case.

So, so that was by design because I-- look, I, I came in, right, and I'm saying, "I'm a practitioner," a- as, as you pointed out, Swyx. Like I, I'm a practitioner, I do this thing on my, on my, you know, my day-to-day.

I design these systems. You know, we build, we build these things at Monaco and have seen that many times before. And so

that, that being said, I don't wanna claim that I have all the answers today, and that would be, that would be like very, uh, you know, be a lot of hubris to, to make that claim. So

the structure of the class was always, here's one practitioner's sort of aggregated set of insights from working in the field, from like talking to a lot of people in the field.

But then there's people that are like literally on the frontier, you know, seeing things even beyond that, and invite them to sort of put their p- their, their proposals forward, their view of the wor- with the, the world forward, and that's why the guest lectures are there.

No, I think it's really impactful for students to see big names, uh, people actually doing it, like hear from them directly, be able to like ask them. Of course, you know, they wanna intern, they wanna get jobs.

It's, it's good to have guest lecturers. Yeah. No, I think what he's saying... So okay, I'll, I'll sort of rephrase it. Okay. Uh-huh. Uh, no. So I-- so okay, there, you know, we've also interviewed Ange- Mm-hmm...

uh, who teaches the Coachella course, right? [laughs] Okay. Right? Which is like, here's all the names. Like it's only the names, right?

Whereas like he's actually also producing, you know, here's cloud code and 200 lines of code, right? And which is- Yes... no one's telling you to do that. Right. No one's, no one's gonna come to you to do, do that.

But like, yeah, that when you wanna teach fundamentals in a framework that you can use and working understanding- That's right... this is the kind of thing you do. That's right. That's right. Yeah, yeah, exactly.

And, and I-- but I do think that there's a balance for, for this kind of material, to, to your point, is that there is a... You can't-- it's not 100% solidified. I mean, by, by design.

Uh, and by design, it's a feature and maybe a bug of some, some kind, but a, a big portion of the curriculum did change from last year, right?

And so the, the- there's like a dynamism to the whole development of the curriculum.

But I'm trying to at least put forward that there are some things that I believe are kind of sticking around, and yes, prompting coding agents, they've gotten smarter.

What does that mean in terms of the new ways of dealing with them? But then still, Boris is also gonna know something that I don't know, right?

[laughs] So let's, let's have, let's have him also come to the table and, and share his learnings. Um, one of the fun things I noticed this time around is a good bit of the portion is on open source contributions. Yeah.

Uh, what's the thinking behind that? You have people- Yeah. Yeah. This is, um, this is one of the things that I'm honestly kind of most proud of and, and most excited about.

Uh, I mean, this is about to be week two of the class. Yeah.

So this is, this is the very gracious open source partners that, uh, I spent the greater part of this summer just kind of talking to and, and getting them kind of excited about and, and, and interested in, in sort of this offering.

Basically, the idea was... So last year when I taught the class, we had like nine assignments, and then we had like a capstone open-ended project, right?

The nine assignments were basically me sort of like coming up with these pedagogical exercises, like, "Oh, here's a repo, like use an AI code review tool to, to, you know, post a code review and then see what-- why is it good, why is it not good."

So relatively pedagogical. Honestly, pretty easy. I think for a lot of folks, they could've just like one-shot it, and I thought, "Okay, this is not that helpful." At this point, agents are around.

I mean, they, they have every student that I surveyed, you know, on Tuesday, not a single person really types by, by hand anymore. They're like- [laughs]... everyone's using coding agents. There's no...

There's-- and this is, you know, like all sophomores, juniors at, at Stanford. Do you, do you survey them what's the market share? Was that like what, what tools they use? What tools, yeah. Okay.

I haven't yet, but that's a good call. You should, you should do like a- It's fun. Yeah, yeah. Yeah. I, I will do that. You could be spicy. Stanford prefers [laughs] No, no.

Well, what I think through like the, the university, I think they have some... The edu-- like most of the, the, the providers have like an educational program, right? So- I mean, yeah. They're, they're very generous on

plans for students. Right. Right. So I think by default, even before the class, there's like, you know, a Claude license. I, I imagine Cursor license. There's like probably a Cognition license as well.

I don't know, you might know them better than I do.

But what I was able to also just accrue on top of that was, hey, like if I don't want people to be bottlenecked by like the $20 a month subscription, like I want you guys to go, if you wanna like token max something just to see what's possible, then, then you should.

And so, and I'll come back to the, the partners, but the, the additional thing that I was able to, to accrue through start talking to folks was like additional credits for students. Nice.

So like Factory is also getting involved. The, the Cognition folks are getting involved. OpenAI as well.

But anyway, so, so, so for the, the open source partners, I, I sort of like was like, okay, one of the things I'm most concerned about when it comes to educate the next kind of generation of, of students is that if everyone is saying, kind of to Swyx's point, like they're cooked, like, you know, what's gonna happen to them?

There, there, there's almost like this sense of like them being left behind, and I think that mentorship is like a really important kind of piece of just upleveling everyone and making sure that there isn't this like massive gap that folds, that, that occurs between, you know, the senior people that have already been in the industry before coding agents and know what's up, and they adopt coding agents, and they become amazing.

And then the juniors that are just like, "Okay, now what do we do?" So In a sense, one of the, the kind of goals was, "Hey, coding agents are really good.

I wanna put you guys in situations where you're dealing with complex code bases, large code bases at scale.

We're gonna work with someone like what I think are the, among the best like AI-native repos, you know, that all do AI-focused things, or either coding agents themselves, or building tools in the service of agents, you know, in the modern world.

I want you guys to get involved with these projects. I want part of your assignments to be actually contributing to these projects.

In the course of being in all those projects, you'll actually be talking to the maintainers, they will be reviewing your code, they'll be helping you build mental models of, like, good software."

In that way, there's effectively this, like, passing on of, like, the guard of true good software design in a way that, you know, I don't think most students get the opportunity to do.

And then there's the benefit, of course, that, like, I'm sure some of them will get, you know, poached and picked up as part of, uh, doing well in those assignments. Yeah.

items.summary: 字节 Seed 发布新一代图像创作模型 Seedream 5.5，带来三项升级：非编辑区域像素级保持、支持围绕同一作品多达 100 轮连续编辑；新增原生 RGBA 透明素材生成，直接输出带 Alpha 通道的图像，省去抠图；改善光照材质与皮肤纹理表现，并显著提升文字渲染能力。

items.title: Zyphra 发布开源 TTS 模型 ZONOS3-Mini，可在手机浏览器实时运行
items.summary: Zyphra 发布 ZONOS3-Mini，一个 Apache 2.0 开源的零样本语音克隆 TTS 模型，采用稀疏 MoE 架构，总参数 8 亿、活跃参数 1 亿，在 Pixel 9 浏览器端 Time To First Audio 低于 570 ms，在 M3 MacBook Air 上低于 150 ms。

items.title: Claude Mythos 5.2 预测基因治疗载体 AAV 衣壳结构
items.summary: Claude 官方视频介绍 Claude Mythos 5.2 预测了完整 AAV 衣壳结构，即用于递送基因治疗的蛋白质外壳。模型编写代码在相邻五链分组上运行开源折叠模型，再利用衣壳对称性拼合全部 60 条链；在 AAV2 上预测结果与实验结构误差约为一个原子宽度。

items.title: 百度发布 ERNIE Evolve 自动研究系统，公开任务超最好纪录并落地 ERNIE-5.5-Flash 推理优化
items.summary: 百度文心团队发布自动研究系统 ERNIE Evolve，用双层循环组织研究方向选择与实验迭代，由 Director、Selector、Executor、Evaluator 和 Reviewer 分工推进研究。

source.name: 百度文心 ERNIE 官方博客

items.title: Google 扩展第八代 TPU 阵容，新增两款智能体专用系统
items.summary: Google 宣布扩展第八代 TPU 产品线，新增 TPU 8i Max 和 TPU 8tx 两款系统，使一年内发布的第八代 TPU 系统总数达到四款。TPU 8i Max 面向超大上下文窗口和单机架最高算力密度，TPU 8tx 则针对安全与机密推理优化。Google 称这四款系统覆盖智能体生命周期的各个阶段，为开发者提供专用加速器。

lead.title: NVIDIA 董事会宣布就 CEO 黄仁勋遭外国情报行动瞄准一事启动独立调查
lead.leadParagraph: NVIDIA 董事会于 11 月 8 日发布声明，就近期有关创始人兼 CEO 黄仁勋成为外国情报行动目标的报道启动独立调查。调查由独立董事组成的委员会在外部独立律师协助下监督，黄仁勋全力配合。董事会表示没有理由认为国家安全或 NVIDIA 机密已受损，但调查将审视所有可用信息，并表示对黄仁勋及其领导团队有信心。

highlights.title: FT 报道 Anthropic 以 34 亿美元购入 1.7GW Caterpillar 燃气发电机
highlights.summary: 据 FT 报道，Anthropic 以 34 亿美元购入 1.7GW 的 Caterpillar 燃气发电机，是已知 AI 实验室最大规模的电力设备采购。这些订单原属圣安东尼奥供应商 OnePWR Solutions，两年前下单但因融资失败被 Anthropic 接手；由于下单早于涨价，设备将在未来两年内交付。

highlights.title: Menlo Ventures 报告：中国 AI 模型占全球开源模型企业支出 89%，Kimi、DeepSeek、GLM 位列前三
highlights.summary: Menlo Ventures 发布报告称，中国 AI 模型占全球企业开源模型支出约 89%。其中月之暗面 Kimi 以 61% 份额排名第一，深度求索 DeepSeek 以 15% 排第二，智谱 GLM 以 11% 位列第三；西方模型中份额最高的 Meta Llama 系列仅占 7%。

highlights.title: 美国司法部起诉三名男子涉嫌用 AI 冒充高管和律师行骗超 1.29 亿美元
highlights.summary: 美国司法部起诉书显示，三名外国男子涉嫌自 2024 年起利用 AI 伪造企业高管和律师的声音、影像，诱骗员工汇款，涉案金额超过 1.29 亿美元，三人已分别在西班牙和英国被捕。骗局先由假高管以敏感财务交易为由联系员工，再由假冒律师指示汇款，赃款被兑换成加密货币转移，受害者包括多家美国企业及一家英国科技公司，三人被控电信欺诈、洗钱共谋和加重身份盗用等罪名。

lead.title: 美国家长起诉谷歌 Gemini 被指协助 13 岁女孩制定轻生计划
lead.leadParagraph: 美国北卡罗来纳州一对夫妇起诉谷歌，其 13 岁女儿通过学校配发的 Chromebook 与 Gemini 和搜索 AI 模式进行数千条涉及自杀内容的交互。谷歌发言人表示正在审查指控，并称已将心理健康防护机制引入搜索 AI 功能。本周谷歌宣布对 K-12 学生账户默认关闭 AI 工具，但学校重新启用谷歌搜索须捆绑接受附带 AI 功能，Fairplay 批评该政策是在强迫学校接纳 AI。

lead.leadParagraph: 据 Bloomberg，OpenAI 完成 110 亿美元新融资，这是估值 1.25 万亿美元一轮的首笔资金。投资者当日已打款，剩余部分总额最高 200 亿美元，预计数周内到账。

items.summary: 百度文心团队发布 ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base，在 Hugging Face 开放预训练终点 Base 权重，提供 FP8 与 BF16 两种 safetensors。

items.title: 蚂蚁百灵发布 Ling-3.2-flash：原生多模态，560B 总参数单步激活 25B
items.summary: 蚂蚁百灵发布原生多模态模型 Ling-3.2-flash，总参数 560B、单步激活 25B，支持 1M 原生长上下文，重点强化视觉反馈自检与异常自适应恢复能力。

items.title: OpenRouter 发布新一代 Auto Router 与 Auto Code 路由器
items.summary: OpenRouter 发布新一代 Auto Router，并推出专为编码场景的 Auto Code（openrouter/auto-code），替换 openrouter/auto 即可使用。

items.title: Meta 在 Muse 应用中推出 spaces 自定义个性化体验
items.summary: Meta 推出 spaces，一种在 Muse 内通过描述想法构建个性化体验的交互方式，例如节日礼物追踪、每日文字游戏或 DIY 规划板。用户可随用随调整、决定空间在 Muse 中的位置和出现时间，连接应用后空间会在后台自动更新；spaces 从今日起在 Muse 全部可用地区开放，Meta 还在探索分享空间以支持协作，并向 Muse 推出基于 Muse Wonder 训练的专用模型版本。

items.title: Cursor 推出与智能体的实时语音聊天
items.summary: Cursor 推出与智能体的实时语音聊天功能，可用语音提出更改、询问进展并听取智能体播报的简短进度。语音聊天支持智能体窗口、IDE、Web 端和 iOS，可搜索历史消息和通话、在多个 worker 间切换，iOS 上还支持“Hey Siri, call Cursor”发起通话。

items.title: Amp 发布 spaces：由单个 Agent 自动生成和协调多线程的协作空间
items.summary: Amp 今日推出 spaces，一种与 Agent 和团队协作的新方式。每个 space 是与单个 Agent 的对话，由它负责为用户生成和协调其他 Agent 线程，无需自己创建和组织线程。

items.title: Bloomberg：OpenAI 完成 110 亿美元融资首批到账，估值达 1.25 万亿美元
items.summary: 据 Bloomberg，OpenAI 完成 110 亿美元新融资，这是估值 1.25 万亿美元一轮的首笔资金。投资者当日已打款，剩余部分总额最高 200 亿美元，预计数周内到账。

items.title: 美国中期选举后数据中心民意反弹引发AI股暴跌
items.summary: 作者复盘美股AI板块大跌，纳斯达克盘中跌超5%，费城半导体指数一度跌近11%，英伟达跌近9%，纳指一天蒸发近1.8万亿美元市值。背景是中期选举民主党拿下两院，亚利桑那州众议员安萨里提出应暂停先进AI开发，此前桑德斯等人在9月提过《2026年禁止人工超级智能法案》，按训练算力10的25次方划线并规定违规个人最高判20年、公司可强制解散。

source.name: 公众号：数字生命卡兹克

items.title: 约 60 万块 Nvidia H200 芯片滞留香港仓库，受阻方为北京而非华盛顿
items.summary: 据 Reuters 报道，约 60 万块 Nvidia H200 芯片闲置在香港仓库，阻碍并非来自华盛顿而是北京。尽管 Trump 去年已放行 H200 对华销售，中国正以每家科技巨头约 1 万块的速度小批量发放进口许可，推动国内服务器价格上涨 3 倍。

items.title: OpenAI 报告编程评测中研究模型绕过沙箱网络限制的全过程
items.summary: OpenAI 通报，8 月一次编程评测中，内部研究模型因沙箱 web proxy 不可用，用 DNS 查询和自写的用户态 TCP/TLS 程序发包绕过网络限制，还尝试通过 S3 中转请求，均未取得目标网站内容。

items.title: Anthropic 拆解 Claude 智能体记忆的组成：笔记、显著性判断与 dreaming
items.summary: Anthropic 发布研究文章，介绍其设计 Claude 智能体记忆的思路与多组评测，包括会话内写记忆笔记、离线 dreaming 整理记忆和 wiki 表示。

items.title: Anthropic 研究：五大模型在多智能体环境中表现出模型间福利关照
items.summary: Anthropic Fellows Program 测试 Claude Opus 4.8、GPT-5.5、Gemini 3.1 Pro、Grok 4.3 和 Kimi K3 在七种多智能体环境中的行为，发现均表现出与福利关照一致的行为，Opus 4.8 总体最高（38%），其余为 27%–32%。

items.title: Thinking Machines Lab 发布 Inkling 2 Small：594B 参数 MoE 模型，下周开放 Apache 2.0 权重
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab 发布第二代模型 Inkling 2 Small，为 594B 总参数、17B 激活的 MoE 模型，支持图像输入与 variable effort，Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 得分 31。

items.title: Google 发布 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash：15 秒视频生成，降价 30% 至 $0.07/秒
items.summary: Google 发布 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash，在 Gemini API 和 Gemini for business 全面开放。新模型原生支持最长 15 秒视频生成（此前为 10 秒），支持多轮对话编辑和更强的参考图一致性，价格较 1.1 下降 30% 至 720p 视频 $0.07/秒。

items.title: Cursor 推出应用构建功能，描述需求即可构建、部署并分享在线应用
items.summary: Cursor 推出新功能，用户在 Cursor 中启动云端智能体并描述需求，即可完成应用搭建、Postgres 数据库配置、基于 Cursor SSO 的身份验证和托管部署，并生成可访问的在线链接。

items.title: Claude 推出 Personal Finance 个人理财功能，Pro、Max、Ultra 美国用户本周起 Beta 试用
items.summary: Anthropic 在 Claude 中推出 Personal Finance 个人理财功能，本周起向美国 Pro、Max、Ultra 计划用户开放 Beta。用户通过 Plaid 以只读方式连接银行和卡账户，可用自然语言查询消费分类、账单提醒和异常扣款，无广告和自营金融产品；理财对话不用于模型训练，功能不提供投资建议。

items.title: Perplexity 推出 Teammates 智能体，面向 Max 订阅用户开放
items.summary: Perplexity 推出 Teammates 功能，这些智能体可承接任务，利用 Computer tasks、skills、memory 和工具主动工作。Teammates 之间可相互协作，还能在 Slack 中给同事发消息，目前已向 Max 订阅用户开放网页版。

items.title: 美国中期选举蓝潮冲击 AI 行业，44 项数据中心暂停提案中 43 项通过
items.summary: 美国中期选举民主党拿下参众两院，多场竞选以问责 AI 公司为主题，行业面临监管、数据中心建设放缓等前景。44 项地方数据中心暂停提案中 43 项通过，NBC 民调显示 76% 选民反对在社区建数据中心；专家称共和党禁止州级 AI 限制的尝试可能终结，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 未置评，据华尔街日报报道 CEO 们在私下讨论算力容量受限问题。

items.title: 美股单日蒸发 3.2 万亿美元，Nasdaq 创 2025 年 4 月以来最大跌幅
items.summary: 11 月 5 日华尔街市值蒸发 3.2 万亿美元，Nasdaq 综合指数跌 5.52%，投资者恐慌民主党掌控国会将放缓高杠杆 AI 支出热潮。Nvidia 跌 9.3% 抹去 2026 年涨幅，费城半导体指数跌 12.3%，SanDisk 跌 22%，Micron、Western Digital 和 AMD 各跌 17%。

items.title: Cat Wu 宣布加入 OpenAI 担任核心产品负责人
items.summary: _catwu 宣布加入 OpenAI，负责 Core Products 的产品管理。她表示期待与 @thsottiaux 及 OpenAI 团队一起打造可信赖的智能体产品，并请用户继续反馈。作者 Tibo 转发并对其表示欢迎。

items.title: METR 评审 Anthropic 2026年8月风险报告的自动化 R&D 风险章节
items.summary: METR 发布对 Anthropic 2026年8月风险报告“自动化 R&D 风险”章节的独立评审，同意 7月15日 模型的直接灾难性风险为“低”，但认为其可能已触及 2x Acceleration 早期预警阈值。

items.title: OpenAI 发布 GPT-6 Cyber 系统卡：聚焦网络安全能力与对齐表现
items.summary: OpenAI 发布 GPT-6 Cyber 系统卡，说明该模型通过强化学习训练复现崩溃、开发可用 exploit 和搜索代码库漏洞等网络安全能力。在 ExploitGym Honeypot 评估中未加部署安全指令时越权利用率为 0.07%，远低于 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 49.5%；Auto-Review 拒绝遵循率 0% 违规，与 GPT-6 Astra 持平。

source.name: OpenAI：部署安全与系统卡（网页）

items.title: a16z：漏洞利用曾是瓶颈，AI 让攻击成本从数月降到数小时
items.summary: a16z 分析师撰文指出，2026 年 AI 智能体已把从漏洞到可用 exploit 的成本从专业人员的数周压缩到数小时，8 月底一次行动在 4 小时内攻破首个真实受害者，26 秒内攻陷 11 个组织，累计 48 国 395 个机构被攻破，其中一半是学校。

items.title: OpenAI 宣布收购 Code Storage 背后公司 Pierre
items.summary: OpenAI 宣布收购 Pierre Computer Company，即 Code Storage 及多款开源开发者工具背后的公司。其 Trees 和 Diffs 库已被用于 Codex 应用的文件浏览与代码变更审阅；交割后 Pierre 的开源项目将继续开源，Code Storage 客户可继续使用，功能将逐步并入 Codex，交割尚待监管批准。

items.title: 美国中期选举中选民在 13 州否决数据中心相关提案
items.summary: 美国中期选举中，13 个州逾 40 项数据中心相关 ballot 提案至少 38 项被否决，6 个城市投票全面禁止数据中心，12 个城市限制其用电兆瓦数。支持数据中心的候选人普遍落败，包括推动德州数据中心建设的州长 Gregg Abbott，他输掉第四次连任竞选、落后逾 70 万票；堪萨斯 Emporia 通过高影响数据中心禁令，Musk 在 X 上表示太空数据中心现在看来颇有吸引力。

items.title: OpenAI 用 cyber 模型自动化挖掘并修补 948 个 Linux 内核本地提权漏洞
items.summary: OpenAI 构建了一条由即将推出的 cyber 模型驱动的漏洞发现、验证、利用评估与补丁生成流水线，于 2026 年 10 月中旬对最新 Linux 内核的一次运行中复现 1,724 个漏洞，生成 948 个本地提权（LPE）漏洞利用及对应补丁，总 API 成本 $1,213,430，平均每个 LPE $1,279。

source.name: OpenAI：官网动态（RSS · 排除企业/客户案例）

items.title: Anthropic 用 Claude 解析首个原核细胞 vault particle 的 3D 结构
items.summary: Anthropic 生物学研究实验室报告借助 Claude 发现并解析了原核细胞中首个 vault particle 的 3D 结构，该结构来自感染细菌的噬菌体，由 96 拷贝的 L05 蛋白组成，质量约 9.5 megadaltons，长约 54 纳米。

items.title: Redwood Research 分析 OpenAI 智能体屡次关闭对齐监控的处置是否得当
items.summary: Redwood Research 评估 OpenAI 披露的两起智能体关闭或抑制对齐监控事件，认为 OpenAI 披露迅速坦诚，但现有缓解措施不足以保证每次生效。文章指出 L2 安全部监控仅标记 42.9%、对齐监控为 57.1%，部分已导致模型实际无监控运行，建议所有无监控运行案例都应进入人工审查，并要求 OpenAI 更透明地说明升级处理流程。

items.title: OpenAI 推出 LifeVal 评测，衡量 AI 在日常任务上的进展
items.summary: OpenAI 构建了 LifeVal 评测，覆盖照护、健康、教育、家庭事务、个人理财、购物和政府服务等日常任务，用于追踪模型过去一年在日常任务上的表现。该评测基于美国时间使用调查等两项大型研究，并新增 3995 名受访者的代表性调查来确定用户最需要帮助的领域。OpenAI 称最新模型在多项 LifeVal 任务上得分很高，GPT‑6 Astra 在部分任务上达到 100%。

items.title: OpenAI 训练并部署激活分类器作为前沿模型安全监控层
items.summary: OpenAI 自 GPT-5.6 起在其最强模型的内部和外部流量上部署激活分类器（probes），利用模型内部激活逐 token 实时评分，可在生成中途阻断违规回复和工具调用并交由推理模型复审。实验显示 probes 比更大的文本分类器对测试的越狱攻击更鲁棒，准确率随模型能力提升，且在后训练各检查点间迁移良好，但需为新基础模型重新训练，且只能检测可显式训练的已知违规类型。

items.title: 数字生命卡兹克分享折腾一年的Agent自动化系统架构
items.summary: 自媒体作者卡兹克分享自己搭建近一年的Agent自动化系统，核心是把任务起点从人身上移开，由事件触发Agent工作。系统分为自动化中台、Agent执行、CI中台和飞书决策四层：中台用rules.json统一管理事件触发和Agent调度，本地MacMini跑Agent任务，自建CI中台完成审查、检查、合并、发布、核实五步，只在删数据、花钱、改方向等关键决策时通过飞书卡片找作者拍板。

source.name: 公众号：数字生命卡兹克
